subject: crowned eagle
title: A 2-Million-Year-Old Child's Killer Was Found. It Was a Bird

scenes.text: A child died two million years ago. We found the killer.
In 1924, a skull turned up in South Africa: a three-year-old ape-child, an early human relative.
For decades, the blame went to a leopard or a sabre-toothed cat.
Then scientists studied monkey skulls left by African crowned eagles, and saw a pattern.
Punctures and ragged cuts at the base of the eye sockets. Talon marks.
The Taung Child had them too. Our ancestors were hunted from the sky.

description:
The Taung Child, found in South Africa in 1924, was the first Australopithecus africanus ever described: a child of about three who died roughly two and a half million years ago by current dating (older reports say about two million).
For decades a leopard or sabre-toothed cat was blamed. In 1995 Lee Berger and Ron Clarke proposed an eagle instead, and in 2006 a study of monkeys killed by crowned eagles in Ivory Coast showed what eagle kills look like: punctures and ragged cuts at the base of the eye sockets. Berger re-examined the Taung skull and found the same marks, plus the kind of dent in the skull that eagle prey often carries. An eagle is now the leading explanation.
What would you have guessed: big cat or bird? Comment below.
first_comment: The marks had been on the skull since 1924. Nobody recognised them for over 80 years. Big cat or bird: what would you have guessed?
